name: Summer Solstice Opportunity Scoring Rubric
note: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. Every skill, the xlsx, and the operating-system doc mirror this file. M2 edits weights HERE first, then regenerates mirrors. Changelog at bottom.

kill_gates.label: Can't ship a usable v1 within one build week
Needs licensing/regulatory approval we can't obtain (or unacceptable legal risk)
Realistic build+launch cost exceeds the pooled <$2k budget
Undifferentiated AI wrapper — no workflow ownership, data moat, or switching cost (acquirers treat these as invisible)

No viable payment mechanism — the chosen channel/product has no named way to charge money (e.g., agent skill stores have no payment rail; a skill-store-distributed candidate needs a named monetization mechanism to pass)

Structurally cannot clear a >=50% gross margin at realistic pricing — COGS-heavy inference relative to the price the market bears (every unit of value = frontier tokens), pass-through-dominated economics, or a free-incumbent price ceiling. Judged from the pro-forma at the gate's fidelity level (see economics_ladder note); 50% is the floor, ~75-80% GM is the design target buyers actually price (Flippa GM>75%)

criteria.label: Pain & Urgency
criteria.anchor_5: acute, 'now' problem people actively complain about (high engagement)

criteria.label: Willingness to Pay
criteria.anchor_5: buyers already pay for inferior tools/workarounds

criteria.label: Free Reachability
criteria.anchor_5: a precise $0 channel reaches buyers at scale, with a fast channel clock: low review/moderation latency, a working payment rail, and short time-to-first-100-qualified-users
criteria.anchor_1: no precise channel, or a channel with weeks of review latency / no way to charge
sub_signals: channel review/moderation latency (record it: e.g., Shopify App Store 2-4+ weeks)

criteria.label: Time-to-First-Dollar
criteria.anchor_5: can charge within days of channel-live

criteria.label: Build Feasibility
criteria.anchor_5: trivially agent-native (agent-parity architecture is the default build form), v1 well within a build week
criteria.anchor_1: hard to build or agent-native architecture awkward for this problem

criteria.label: Natural Retention
criteria.anchor_5: recurring job-to-be-done (weekly/monthly), product accumulates data or workflow lock-in that compounds — the category retains by nature
criteria.anchor_1: one-shot job (migration, generator); user leaves when done
criteria.rationale: Every financial buyer gates on churn; this selects for categories that CAN retain before we ever measure it

criteria.label: Market Adequacy
criteria.anchor_5: enough buyers to reach ~$250k+ ARR, niche enough to win
criteria.anchor_1: too small to matter or too broad to win

criteria.label: Acquirability
criteria.anchor_5: recurring revenue + high switching cost + owner-independent/transferable + clean asset; bonus if adjacent to a named acquirer whose minimums we can realistically meet (check the age/TTM reality flags in Acquirer-Intelligence.md) AND whose appetite for this exact asset class is evidenced by a specific portfolio company or deal (cite it — a famous buyer name without portfolio adjacency scores as no named buyer; classify thesis-buyer vs size-class buyer vs plan-of-record venue per the buyer-map note in Acquirer-Intelligence.md)
criteria.anchor_1: one-off revenue, founder-dependent, no plausible buyer

criteria.label: Competitive Wedge
criteria.anchor_5: clear underserved gap + defensible angle in an un-crowded or genuinely differentiable space — CITED FROM AN S4 POSITIONING TEARDOWN, not vibes
criteria.requires: S4 positioning-teardown output for any finalist; Wedge <= 3 triggers the mandatory S5 switch test

verdicts.strong: >=75 and all gates pass -> advance to S5 (a passing score is necessary, not sufficient)
verdicts.conditional: 60-74 -> pursue only if the pipeline is thin

notes: Agent-native is the DEFAULT ARCHITECTURE we build in (agent parity, atomic tools, features-as-prompts) — it is scored in Build Feasibility and Acquirability anchors, NOT a kill gate. We don't auto-reject opportunities whose buyers don't price it. (Owner decision, July 2026, per External Review #01.)
Wedge <= 3 candidates can NEVER pass S5 on Tier-1 category evidence alone — a switch test is mandatory (see demand-confidence-gate).
M2 weight edits require n>=3 logged outcomes; structural changes (gates added/removed) require n>=5 or an unambiguous external fact.

ECONOMICS LADDER (owner directive, 2026-07-06): a pro-forma is part of the assessment at EVERY gate, at increasing fidelity — S0: coarse COGS-intensity class + GM band per seed (inference-light workflow / per-unit document parsing / inference-core); S2: mini pro-forma (price anchor from named competitors, COGS/unit incl. tokens, GM%) feeding the margin_floor gate; S4: pricing corridor vs incumbents + refined unit economics; S6: v1 pro-forma in the Build Brief (pricing, COGS model, token-budget guardrails: model routing, caching, metering, BYO-key) + per-customer COGS instrumentation as an acceptance item; S15: actuals vs pro-forma weekly.

BUYER MAP (owner directive, 2026-07-06): Acquirer-Intelligence.md is a directory, not a per-deal answer. Every candidate needs an OPPORTUNITY-SPECIFIC buyer map: named buyers justified by a specific portfolio asset/deal (e.g., Visma via its Link My Books acquisition, for an e-commerce accounting tool), classified as thesis-buyer / size-class buyer / plan-of-record venue, each with the MRR/age milestone at which it becomes reachable. S0 requires the citation; S4 validates the map for finalists.

changelog.change: exit-first: added Acquirability weight-up, wrapper gate
M2 calibration #1 (rehearsal): Wedge 4->10, Pain 18->16, Reachability 18->14 — saturation was under-penalized

External Review #01: added Natural Retention (10) funded by TTFD 12->8, Market Adequacy 6->4, Reachability 14->12, Build Feasibility 12->10; agent-native kill gate removed (now default-architecture + anchors); added no-payment-rail gate; channel-latency sub-signals; Wedge must cite S4 teardown; rubric made machine-readable single source

Owner directive (external review of a live cycle — structural change authorized by owner, outside M2's n>=5 self-calibration rule): added margin_floor kill gate (>=50% GM structural floor) + economics-ladder note (pro-forma at every gate, fidelity rising S0->S15); Acquirability anchor tightened to require portfolio-evidenced named buyers (opportunity-specific buyer map, thesis vs size-class vs venue). Trigger: an external economics + acquirer-fit review of a live candidate (a well-known buyer had been named without portfolio adjacency; the margin question had gone unasked by the system)
